profile.name: Jack Zorola
profile.headline: Operations leader who builds the machine
profile.pitch: Ten years building the internal machinery of growing companies: new divisions from zero, processes that survive the founder, and AI that actually lands in regulated operations, with numbers.
profile.location: Monterrey, Mexico · Remote · US time-zone overlap

projects.title: A new revenue line, built inside other people's hospitals
projects.tagline: Five hospital partners, each site live in 30 days, growth 8× the hospital's own management.
projects.summary: Case study + tool: the revenue-share model with an endless aisle, a 30-day launch plan with a go-live gate, a ramp simulator, a deal calculator for in-hospital pharmacies, and the point of sale I co-designed because the platform couldn't run a store.

projects.title: A company that survives losing anyone
projects.tagline: A documentation operating system with an AI judge, built so any process survives its owner leaving.
projects.summary: Template + tool: one master doc per area, one doc per process with a mandatory continuity section, governance by folder ownership, an append-only decision log, and an AI review protocol. Run the judge and the truck test on a fictional company, then download the starter kit.

projects.title: AI adoption that showed up in the hiring plan
projects.tagline: A company-wide AI program for 30 people, and the readiness model I built after the one team that never adopted it.
projects.summary: Case study and tool: a five-step playbook, an interactive value × readiness prioritization model (v1, what I used, vs v2, what I'd use now), a week-one readiness checklist, and the session-brief format behind every 1:1.

projects.title: The nightly job that could erase weeks of sales work
projects.tagline: Rafónica's data model: robots own the data, people own the relationship, privacy is checked before every write.
projects.summary: Case study + tool from my own startup: a two-axis state model, gates written as filters, consent-first inventory and a fail-closed privacy exclusion. Play the one-field vs two-axis simulator, send a privacy request, and see why reach uses the median.

projects.title: Invoice reconciliation, without the hire
projects.tagline: 4 hours a day of matching stock to supplier invoices, brought down to minutes.
projects.summary: Case study and working code: a CFDI (Mexican e-invoice) parser and a goods-received ↔ invoice matcher with per-supplier folio rules, confidence scoring and a human review queue.

projects.title: Slack birthday bot on Airtable
projects.tagline: Replaced a paid bot with the HR table the team already had.
projects.summary: One scheduled Airtable script and a tiny Slack app: weekend logic, fair message rotation, self-recovery after a failed day, and a daily token health check. Interactive simulator included.

ventures.name: Rafónica
ventures.what: A marketplace that connects nano and micro content creators with local businesses that have never done influencer marketing, so both sides know exactly what they are buying and selling.
built: Discovery and measurement pipeline: 200+ creators measured on real reach, not follower counts
Consent first: nobody is sellable without a signed agreement; 6 signed, e-signature included
CRM of ~12,000 local businesses built from open government data
Published privacy notice with a working opt-out, and encrypted off-site backups with a tested restore

ventures.name: La Consultoría
ventures.role: Partner, taking over from the founder
ventures.what: Health-regulatory consulting in Mexico: COFEPRIS licensing for pharmacies and warehouses, validations, and ISO 9001, backed by the founder's 30 years of experience.
built: Website, SEO and a blog pipeline from research to publication
A new service line: fractional operations, processes and AI for small businesses
Knowledge transfer from a 30-year founder into documented, repeatable services

ventures.name: LunaSurfer
ventures.what: Ticketing for independent bands: the band sells its own tickets and keeps almost all the money; venues lend dead hours and keep the bar.
built: Multi-tenant platform: band profile, event page, checkout
Payments with Stripe Connect, live with real money
QR check-in at the door with atomic ticket validation
Migrated from a no-code prototype (Airtable + Make) to its own platform
